---
title: "GWAS-Assisted Best Linear Unbiased Prediction (GWABLUP)"
---

## GWAS-Assisted Best Linear Unbiased Prediction (GWABLUP) {.unnumbered}


### Description

Genomic prediction using GWAS-weighted relationship matrix.
Implements Meuwissen et al. (2024) GWABLUP: weights all markers
by their posterior probability of having non-zero effects,
derived from EMMAX GWAS results.



### Usage

<pre><code class='language-R'>gwablup(
  y,
  markers,
  gwas_result,
  X = NULL,
  method = "auto",
  solver = "auto",
  max_iter = 100L,
  tol = 1e-06,
  n_threads = NULL,
  min_weight = 1e-04,
  ref_markers = NULL,
  trait = "continuous",
  link = "logit"
)
</code></pre>


### Arguments

<table>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="y">y</code></td>
<td>
numeric named vector of phenotypes (length n)
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="markers">markers</code></td>
<td>
list of raw marker inputs:


<ul>
<li> <code>snp_add</code>: matrix (n x m), raw genotype 0/1/2

</li>
<li> <code>mh_add</code>: list of chr data.frames

</li></ul>
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="gwas_result">gwas_result</code></td>
<td>
object of class <code>"gwas_result"</code> from
<code>run_gwas()</code>. Must be run with the same markers and individuals.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="X">X</code></td>
<td>
fixed effects design matrix (n x c). If NULL, intercept only
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="method">method</code></td>
<td>
character, REML algorithm (default &quot;auto&quot;).
Passed to <code>masreml()</code>
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="solver">solver</code></td>
<td>
character, EBV solver (default &quot;auto&quot;).
Passed to <code>masreml()</code>
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="max_iter">max_iter</code></td>
<td>
integer, maximum REML iterations (default 100)
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="tol">tol</code></td>
<td>
numeric, convergence tolerance (default 1e-6)
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="n_threads">n_threads</code></td>
<td>
integer, number of threads (default: all cores)
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="ref_markers">ref_markers</code></td>
<td>
list of raw marker data for training individuals only,
same format as <code>markers</code>. If provided, allele frequencies for
building G_wa are computed from <code>ref_markers</code> instead of
<code>markers</code>. Use in train/test context to avoid data leakage.
If NULL (default), allele frequencies computed from <code>markers</code>.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="trait">trait</code></td>
<td>
character, trait distribution: <code>"continuous"</code> (default)
or <code>"binary"</code>. Passed to <code>masreml()</code>.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="link">link</code></td>
<td>
character, link function for binary trait: <code>"logit"</code>
(default) or <code>"probit"</code>. Passed to <code>masreml()</code>.
</td></tr>
</table>


### Details

User workflow:


<ol>
<li> Fit standard GBLUP: <code>fit &lt;- masreml(y, markers)</code>

</li>
<li> Run GWAS: <code>gwas &lt;- run_gwas(markers, y, fit)</code>

</li>
<li> Inspect GWAS results (optional): <code>summary(gwas)</code>

</li>
<li> Run GWABLUP: <code>fit_wa &lt;- gwablup(y, markers, gwas)</code>

</li></ol>



### Value

Object of class <code>c("gwablup", "masreml")</code> —
identical structure to <code>masreml()</code> output, with
additional <code>\$gwas</code> slot containing the gwas_result.
All S3 methods from masreml (summary, print, plot) work directly.



### References

Meuwissen et al. (2024) GWABLUP: genome-wide association
assisted BLUP. <em>Genet Sel Evol.</em> 56:17.



### See Also

<code>masreml</code>, <code>run_gwas</code>,
<code>compute_accuracy</code>



### Examples
```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval=FALSE}
library("masreml")

# ── SNP GWABLUP ───────────────────────────────────────────
fit    <- masreml(y, markers = list(snp_add = W))
gwas   <- run_gwas(markers = list(snp_add = W), y = y, masreml_fit = fit)
fit_wa <- gwablup(y, markers = list(snp_add = W), gwas_result = gwas)
summary(fit_wa)

# ── MH GWABLUP ────────────────────────────────────────────
fit    <- masreml(y, markers = list(mh_add = mh_list))
gwas   <- run_gwas(markers = list(mh_add = mh_list), y = y, masreml_fit = fit)
fit_wa <- gwablup(y, markers = list(mh_add = mh_list), gwas_result = gwas)
summary(fit_wa)

# ── Compare GBLUP vs GWABLUP ──────────────────────────────
fit_gblup   <- masreml(y, markers = list(snp_add = W))
gwas        <- run_gwas(list(snp_add = W), y, fit_gblup)
fit_gwablup <- gwablup(y, list(snp_add = W), gwas)
cor(fit_gblup$total_gebv, fit_gwablup$total_gebv)

# ── Train/test workflow (no data leakage) ─────────────────
fit_tr  <- masreml(y_train, markers = list(snp_add = W_train))
gwas_tr <- run_gwas(
  markers     = list(snp_add = W_train),
  y           = y_train,
  masreml_fit = fit_tr,
  ref_markers = list(snp_add = W_train)
)
fit_wa_tr <- gwablup(
  y           = y_train,
  markers     = list(snp_add = W_train),
  gwas_result = gwas_tr,
  ref_markers = list(snp_add = W_train)
)

# ── Binary trait GWABLUP ──────────────────────────────────
fit_tr_bin <- masreml(y_bin_train, markers = list(snp_add = W_train),
                      trait = "binary")
gwas_bin   <- run_gwas(list(snp_add = W_train), y_bin_train, fit_tr_bin,
                       ref_markers = list(snp_add = W_train))
fit_wa_bin <- gwablup(y_bin_train, list(snp_add = W_train), gwas_bin,
                      trait = "binary", ref_markers = list(snp_add = W_train))
G_full <- build_G_snp(W_all, ref_W = W_train)
pred   <- predict(fit_wa_tr,
                  G_full    = list(snp_add = G_full),
                  train_ids = rownames(W_train),
                  test_ids  = rownames(W_test))




```
